title: Accurate and Efficient World Modeling with Masked Latent Transformers
summary: A current-release episode-boundary mask can ignore cached reset flags and reintroduce prior-episode attention values. The release also differs from the paper in KL clipping/weighting, imagination batch size and decoder channels. Public aggregate results remain supported; historical experiment binding and stronger causal claims need evidence.
limitations: Source commit 665948d8cd619ccc960abe54ffdfc785ce95f18b is the acquired public release, not verified as the historical experiment commit.
No author code imported/executed, environment run, trained checkpoint or timing reproduction.
All 19 pages read as text, including actual appendices despite manifest flag; selected source pages 9, 13, 18 and 19 visually inspected.
Selected central source files reviewed; not every one of 82 files or third-party dependency.
No per-seed historical logs, human person/episode data, full Atari setup, or acquired separate supplement.

claim.location: PDF pp. 5-6 Section 3.1; pinned nnet/modules/emerald/tssm.py lines 341-363 and 459-481; main model env_step and WorldModel.forward; attention_mask.py
claim.text: Cached past context should retain same-episode history while excluding earlier trajectories.

assumptions: All current is_firsts flags zero; cached reset flag is nonzero.
Old-episode K/V remain in the finite cache; causal window includes them.
Equal attention logits and an old nonzero value component are valid attention parameters/inputs.
problems.check: The current-only guard skips the cached episode mask. Minimal masks [1,1,1] versus [0,1,1] give attention 2/3 versus 0; full 64-entry cache gives 2/65 versus 0.
problems.result: Previous-episode values can influence current hidden state after a reset has moved into cached context.
counterevidence: imagine applies cached reset masking when flags are supplied.
play creates a fresh cache each evaluation episode.
Historical five-seed code identity remains unknown.
problems.impact: Localized episode-isolation defect in released training/collection, with a possible state-distribution discrepancy. Fresh-state direct evaluation and correct imagine masking limit the demonstrated scope. Material core-conclusion harm and historical attribution remain unestablished.
problems.correction: Apply episode-separation masking whenever cached/current reset information exists; reset current states/actions separately, or clear old cache per environment.
problems.core_dependency: Episode separation in the released cached temporal-state path.
problems.severity_rationale: Minor: exact cached-reset mask defect is localized to the boundary path; fresh-state direct evaluation and correct imagine masking limit the demonstrated core impact.

acceptance_check.scope: No historical experiment binding or material core conclusion effect established; neither false theorem nor benchmark loss is imposed as a prerequisite.

clarifications.location: PDF p. 7 score definition and Table5 p. 13
clarifications.detail: Rounded human rates give52.0497 (rounding interval51.9822-52.1123) rather than50.5. Per-person score averaging can explain a nonlinear aggregation gap; raw protocol is unavailable. Agent ordering survives either reference.

Spatial layout and MaskGIT change together and RSSM sizes differ. Spatial TSSM outperforms spatial RSSM, while vector TSSM underperforms vector RSSM; spatial TSSM pixel loss is slightly higher. Stronger isolated/architecture-general attribution needs matched controls and seed-level uncertainty.
Need exact five-seed configurations/checkpoints, individual outcomes, evaluation aggregation order, Atari settings and timing logs. Public twenty-seed aggregate is a separate release result.
